cities: 12 stores across the US, including New York, East Rutherford, Brooklyn, and its own site

craft_evidence.owned: NONE found. Claim only: "Our collections begin in our London atelier" (sketching and draping, i.e. design, not making). No owned factory or mill named on site or in the H&M 2025 annual report.
craft_evidence.makers: NONE: 0 of 29 product pages read name a factory or maker.
craft_evidence.mills: 1 of 29 PDPs (evidence): the Mario Bellucci mill, Prato, on Wool-twill regular-fit tapered pants 1354279. Fibre certifications (RWS TE-00047206 on merino crew 1260173; Good Cashmere Standard on cashmere crew 1291684) are standards, not mills.
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated and placed (evidence): "Since 2007" (cos.com sustainability page); first stores on Regent Street, London, March 2007 (MD Marie Honda, Dezeen, 5 Nov 2014). Brand launched by H&M Group.
craft_evidence.process: General only (claim): cloth "selected for its character, yarn count, fibre length, finish and quality"; PDPs give fabric weights (230gsm tee, 15oz selvedge, 480gsm cashmere) but no making process.
craft_evidence.reasoning: COS owns no making facility; its "London atelier" is a design studio. Of 29 men's product pages read, none states a country of manufacture or names a factory, and one names a cloth mill (Bellucci, Prato). The founding date and place are checkable and two fibre certifications are named, which lifts it just above 1.

ownership.owner: H & M Hennes & Mauritz AB (H&M Group; Nasdaq Stockholm)

opview: “For our customer and our aesthetic, I think the key for us is timelessness, modernity, functionality and tactility.” — Marie Honda, managing director, COS, Dezeen
